raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

`sgl-kernel` cannot be built for Radeon RDNA4 GPUs (`gfx1201`: Radeon AI PRO R9700 / R9600D, RX 9070 series): the target is not in the `setup_rocm.py` allowlist. Adding it to the list is not enough. The MoE TopK routing kernels then fail at launch:

| test (gfx1201, allowlist-only build) | result |
|---|---|
| `test_moe_topk_softmax.py` | `Fatal Python error: Aborted` (core dump) |
| `test_moe_topk_sigmoid.py` | `torch.AcceleratorError: HIP error: unspecified launch failure` |

Root cause: on ROCm, `WARP_SIZE` is the wave size of the code object being compiled. It is 32 in the device pass for gfx1250 / gfx1201, but it is always 64 in the host pass. The TopK host launchers derive the per-thread work (`VPT`), the template instantiation, and `block_dim` from `WARP_SIZE`. For wave32 targets the host therefore launches the wave64 configuration of a kernel that was compiled for wave32. `gfx1250`, which is already in the allowlist, has the same host/device mismatch. `kvcacheio/transfer.cu` also sizes its blocks with the host-side `WARP_SIZE`.

## Modifications

- `include/utils.h`:
  - Documents what `WARP_SIZE` means on ROCm.
  - Adds `sgl_launch_warp_size()`, the runtime wave size of the current device (from the cached `at::cuda` device properties).
  - Adds `SGL_DISPATCH_WARP_SIZE(...)`, which runs a lambda with `constexpr int kWarpSize` set to 32 or 64.
  - Adds `sgl_wave_matches_target<WAVE>`, which is true when `WAVE` matches the code object being compiled.
  - On CUDA these resolve to `WARP_SIZE` / 32, with no behavior change.
- `moe_topk_softmax_kernels.cu`, `moe_topk_sigmoid_kernels.cu`:
  - `topkGating{Softmax,Sigmoid}` and `TopkConstants` are templated on the wave size, and the launchers dispatch on the device's wave size.
  - Each code object gets both instantiations. Only the one matching its wave size has a body; the other compiles to a 2–5 instruction trap stub and is never launched.
- `kvcacheio/transfer.cu`: on ROCm, `threads_per_block` uses `sgl_launch_warp_size()`.
- `setup_rocm.py`: adds `gfx1201` to `supported_targets`, with comments on wave size, FP8 format (OCP E4M3), and LDS budget.
- `docs/.../amd_gpu.mdx`: adds a "Radeon RDNA4 / gfx1201 (experimental)" section covering build, wave-size rules for kernel authors, and serving notes.

Other wave-size uses were checked and need no change:
- `moe_align`: the host only over-provisions threads, and the ROCm path is independent of wave size.
- `topk.hip` and `deepseek_v4_topk.cu`: wave handling is device-side only.
- `dsv4_norm_rope`: already writes E4M3FN on gfx12.

## Wave64 targets are unchanged

`sgl-kernel` was built from `main` and from this PR for each target (`AMDGPU_TARGET=<arch>`, GPUs hidden), and the disassembled code objects were compared kernel by kernel, ignoring only addresses and symbol names:

| target | kernels compared | identical | extra (other-wave trap stubs) |
|---|---|---|---|
| gfx942 | 215 | 215 | 57 (2 instructions each) |
| gfx950 | 215 | 215 | 57 (2 instructions each) |
| gfx1250 | 215 | 215 | 57 (5 instructions each) |
| gfx1201 | 215 | 215 (vs. allowlist-only build) | 57 |

On gfx942 / gfx950 the device code is therefore unchanged. The runtime cost is one cached device-property lookup per TopK / KV-transfer launch. On gfx1250 the device code is also unchanged, but the host now launches the wave32 configuration it was compiled for; I have no gfx1250 hardware to test this on.

## Accuracy Tests

**Kernel unit tests on R9700 (gfx1201)**, PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0:

| test | allowlist only | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `test_moe_topk_softmax.py` | abort (core dump) | 744 passed |
| `test_moe_topk_sigmoid.py` | `hipErrorLaunchFailure` | 774 passed |
| `test_moe_align.py` | 4368 passed, 72 skipped | 4368 passed, 72 skipped |
| `test_topk.py` | 162 passed, 1 skipped | 162 passed, 1 skipped |
| `test_kvcacheio.py` | 144 passed, 50 skipped | 144 passed, 50 skipped |
| `test_activation.py` | 945 passed | 945 passed |
| `test_dsv4_norm_rope.py` | 16 passed | 16 passed |

**LLM end to end (exercises `sgl_kernel.topk_softmax`):**
- Model and setup: Qwen3-30B-A3B BF16 (128 experts, top-8), TP4 on 4x R9700.
- Flags: `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0 --attention-backend triton --disable-custom-all-reduce`.
- GSM8K (200 questions, 5-shot): accuracy **0.930**, invalid 0.000.
- With the allowlist-only build, the same server fails at startup during CUDA graph capture with `RuntimeError: topk_softmax launch error: unspecified launch failure`.

**Diffusion smoke:** MiniMax-H3 (Ref2AV) with TP2 on 2x R9700 and `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`, using the custom all-reduce fix from #43676, completes 2 denoising steps and writes the video.

## Roadmap: gfx1201 SageAttention / Sol-Attn in SGLang Diffusion

This PR is the first step toward fast MiniMax-H3 (and other DiT) serving on Radeon gfx1201 with SGLang Diffusion. Today, on gfx1201:
- `SAGE_ATTN` and `SOL_ATTN` are rejected on ROCm, because they call CUDA-only packages.
- `AITER_SAGE` runs, but it uses the aiter Triton `fav3_sage` kernel. That kernel takes 12.4 s per MiniMax-H3 attention call, which makes it 3.25x slower end to end than BF16 SDPA (688.3 vs 211.6 s per DiT step).

Two gfx1201 attention ops are being upstreamed to AITER as a four-part series:
- `gfx1201_sage_attention`: INT8 QK^T, FP8 PV, FP32 accumulation; a HIP kernel plus a hand-scheduled code object. It is ROCm/aiter#6390 plus a follow-up.
- `gfx1201_sol_attention`: Sol-Attn block routing with the same arguments as NVlabs `sol_attn`; also HIP plus a code object.
- The overall integration plan for LightX2V, diffusers, vLLM-Omni and SGLang Diffusion is in [this comment on ROCm/aiter#6292](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6292#issuecomment-6106014448).

With these ops plugged into stock LightX2V, MiniMax-H3 ref2av (TP2, 2x R9700, 768x1344, 362 frames, 29 steps) measures:

| attention | DiT s/step | vs BF16 SDPA |
|---|---|---|
| BF16 SDPA | 211.6 | 1.00x |
| aiter Triton `fav3_sage` (today's `AITER_SAGE`) | 688.3 | 0.31x |
| `gfx1201_sage_attention` | 89.1 | 2.38x |
| `gfx1201_sol_attention` (Sol config) | 60.8 | 3.48x |

Planned SGLang changes, in order:

1. This PR: `sgl-kernel` builds and runs correctly on gfx1201 (wave32).
2. #43676: custom all-reduce IPC setup no longer breaks multi-GPU runs on PCIe Radeon with `expandable_segments`.
3. SGLang Diffusion `AITER_SAGE`: dispatch to `gfx1201_sage_attention` on gfx1201, keeping the existing `fav3_sage` path on other archs. This lands after the AITER Sage parts are merged.
4. SGLang Diffusion `SOL_ATTN`: accept it on ROCm through `gfx1201_sol_attention`, with `AITER_SAGE` as the dense guard. This lands after the AITER Sol parts are merged.
5. A gfx1201 CI runner, if maintainers are open to it, so this target stays covered.

Steps 3 and 4 are opt-in and only change behavior on gfx1201. The CUDA and gfx94x/gfx95x paths stay unchanged.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add documentation (`amd_gpu.mdx`).
- [x] Provide accuracy results (above).

---

Latest PR Test (Extra): <!-- slot:pr-test-extra:start -->:x: [Run #38135876782](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/38135876782)<!-- slot:pr-test-extra:end -->

files.patch:
@@ -227,3 +227,35 @@ docker run -it --rm \
 - LLM / SRT: `--attention-backend triton` (or rely on the gfx115 auto-default), `--num-gpus 1`
 - Diffusion / DiT (e.g. Wan2.2): `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`, `--num-gpus 1`
 - Keep `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0` (already set in the official image)
+
+## Radeon RDNA4 / gfx1201 (experimental)
+
+Radeon AI PRO R9700 / R9600D and Radeon RX 9070 / 9070 XT (`gfx1201`) are wave32 RDNA4 discrete GPUs. They are
+not covered by the Instinct/CDNA `rocm.Dockerfile` image or by SGLang CI, so support is experimental. It has been
+checked on Radeon AI PRO R9700 (32 GB, PCIe) with PyTorch 2.11.0+rocm10.0.0 (HIP runtime 7.15).
+
+**Build `sgl-kernel`** for gfx1201 (`setup_rocm.py` uses the architecture of GPU 0 when a GPU is visible and
+`AMDGPU_TARGET` otherwise):
+
+```bash Command
+cd python/sglang/kernels/aot
+AMDGPU_TARGET=gfx1201 python setup_rocm.py install
+```
+
+**Wave size.** gfx1201 and gfx1250 run 32-lane waves, gfx942 and gfx950 run 64-lane waves. In `sgl-kernel`,
+`WARP_SIZE` is the wave size of the code object being compiled and is only meaningful in device code: the host
+compilation pass always sees 64. Host code that derives launch geometry from the wave size uses
+`sgl_launch_warp_size()`, and kernels whose data layout depends on it are templated on the wave size and launched
+through `SGL_DISPATCH_WARP_SIZE` (see `include/utils.h` and `csrc/moe/moe_topk_softmax_kernels.cu`). For each
+target only the matching instantiation has a body; the other one compiles to a trap, so the gfx942 / gfx950 code
+objects are unchanged.
+
+**Serving notes on gfx1201**:
+
+- Set `SGLANG_USE_AITER=0`; the AITER paths used by SGLang target Instinct (CDNA) GPUs.
+- LLM / SRT: `--attention-backend triton`.
+- Diffusion / DiT: `--attention-backend torch_sdpa`.
+- Multi-GPU: R9700 cards are connected over PCIe, so the custom all-reduce (which needs full XGMI connectivity) is
+  never selected and all-reduce goes through RCCL; `--disable-custom-all-reduce` skips its setup entirely. Multi-GPU
+  runs with `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` (used by SGLang Diffusion) need
+  [#43676](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43676).

@@ -339,6 +339,10 @@ inline bool getEnvEnablePDL() {
 
 #define CEILDIV(x, y) (((x) + (y) - 1) / (y))
 
+// WARP_SIZE is a compile-time constant for device code: on ROCm 64 for CDNA (gfx9) and 32 for the wave32
+// targets (gfx11, gfx12). The host pass of a HIP build is shared by every --offload-arch and always sees 64,
+// so host-side launch geometry must come from sgl_launch_warp_size(), and kernels whose layout depends on
+// the wave size are instantiated per wave size and selected with SGL_DISPATCH_WARP_SIZE.
 #ifndef USE_ROCM
 #define WARP_SIZE 32
 #else
@@ -349,6 +353,47 @@ inline bool getEnvEnablePDL() {
 #endif
 #endif
 
+// False only in a device pass whose wave size differs from WAVE; such instantiations are never launched,
+// so their bodies are dropped instead of being compiled for the wrong wave size.
+#if defined(USE_ROCM) && defined(__HIP_DEVICE_COMPILE__)
+template <int WAVE>
+inline constexpr bool sgl_wave_matches_target = (WAVE == WARP_SIZE);
+#else
+template <int WAVE>
+inline constexpr bool sgl_wave_matches_target = true;
+#endif
+
+#ifdef USE_ROCM
+#include <ATen/cuda/CUDAContext.h>
+
+inline int sgl_launch_warp_size() {
+  return at::cuda::getCurrentDeviceProperties()->warpSize;
+}
+
+// Calls the lambda argument with `constexpr int kWarpSize` equal to the current device's wave size.
+#define SGL_DISPATCH_WARP_SIZE(...)                                            \
+  [&] {                                                                        \
+    const int sgl_warp_size = sgl_launch_warp_size();                          \
+    if (sgl_warp_size == 32) {                                                 \
+      constexpr int kWarpSize = 32;                                            \
+      return (__VA_ARGS__)();                                                  \
+    }                                                                          \
+    TORCH_CHECK(sgl_warp_size == 64, "Unsupported wave size ", sgl_warp_size); \
+    constexpr int kWarpSize = 64;                                              \
+    return (__VA_ARGS__)();                                                    \
+  }()
+#else
+inline int sgl_launch_warp_size() {
+  return WARP_SIZE;
+}
+
+#define SGL_DISPATCH_WARP_SIZE(...)      \
+  [&] {                                  \
+    constexpr int kWarpSize = WARP_SIZE; \
+    return (__VA_ARGS__)();              \
+  }()
+#endif
+
 #ifdef USE_ROCM
 
 #include "hip/hip_math_def.h"

@@ -74,21 +74,25 @@ def _get_version():
 else:
     print(f"Warning: torch.cuda not available. Using default target: {amdgpu_target}")
 
-if amdgpu_target not in ["gfx942", "gfx950", "gfx1250"]:
+# gfx942/gfx950 run 64-lane waves; gfx1250 and gfx1201 (RDNA4) run 32-lane waves. Device code sees the
+# target's wave size in WARP_SIZE, host launch code queries it at runtime (see include/utils.h).
+supported_targets = ["gfx942", "gfx950", "gfx1250", "gfx1201"]
+if amdgpu_target not in supported_targets:
     print(
-        f"Warning: Unsupported GPU architecture detected '{amdgpu_target}'. Expected 'gfx942', 'gfx950', or 'gfx1250'."
+        f"Warning: Unsupported GPU architecture detected '{amdgpu_target}'. Expected one of {supported_targets}."
     )
     sys.exit(1)
 
 fp8_macro = (
     "-DHIP_FP8_TYPE_FNUZ" if amdgpu_target == "gfx942" else "-DHIP_FP8_TYPE_E4M3"
-)  # gfx950 and gfx1250 use E4M3
+)  # gfx950, gfx1250 and gfx1201 use E4M3 (OCP)
 
 # Dynamic shared-memory budget for the TopK kernels.
 # - gfx942 (MI300/MI325): LDS is typically 64KB per workgroup -> keep dynamic smem <= ~48KB
 #   (leaves room for static shared allocations in the kernel).
 # - gfx95x (MI350) and gfx1250: LDS is larger. Large dynamic budget wastes LDS
 #   and pins occupancy to 1 block/CU. Keep it small (40KB) for better occupancy.
+# - gfx1201 (RDNA4): 64KB LDS per workgroup, so the 40KB budget fits as well.
 topk_dynamic_smem_bytes = 48 * 1024 if amdgpu_target == "gfx942" else 40 * 1024
 
 hipcc_flags = [
